ud3.8:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud3.8:1.3: Then at that time, amongst many monks, after returning from the alms-round after the meal, assembling together, and sitting in the Kareri Round Hall, this conversation arose:
ud3.8:2.1: “An alms-gathering monk, venerable friends, while walking for alms gets the opportunity from time to time to see appealing forms with the eye; gets the opportunity from time to time to hear appealing sounds with the ear; gets the opportunity from time to time to smell appealing smells with the nose; gets the opportunity from time to time to taste appealing flavours with the tongue; gets the opportunity from time to time to touch appealing tangibles with the body.
ud3.8:2.2: An alms-gathering monk, venerable friends, walking for alms is venerated, respected, revered, honoured, and esteemed.
ud3.8:2.3: Now, venerable friends, we too should be alms-gatherers,
ud3.8:2.4: and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to see appealing forms with the eye; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to hear appealing sounds with the ear; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to smell appealing smells with the nose; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to taste appealing flavours with the tongue; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to touch appealing tangibles with the body;
ud3.8:2.5: and we also will walk for alms being venerated, respected, revered, honoured, and esteemed.”
ud3.8:2.6: Now this conversation that arose amongst those monks was left unfinished.
ud3.8:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having risen from seclusion in the evening time, went to the Kareri Round Hall, and after going, he sat down on the prepared seat.
ud3.8:3.2: Having sat down the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
ud3.8:3.3: “What is the talk about, monks, amongst those who have assembled at present, and what is the conversation that you left unfinished?”
ud3.8:4.1: “Here, reverend Sir, after returning from the alms-round after the meal, assembling together, and sitting in the Kareri Round Hall, this conversation arose:
ud3.8:5.1: ‘An alms-gathering monk, venerable friends, while walking for alms gets the opportunity from time to time to see appealing forms with the eye; gets the opportunity from time to time to hear appealing sounds with the ear; gets the opportunity from time to time to smell appealing smells with the nose; gets the opportunity from time to time to taste appealing flavours with the tongue; gets the opportunity from time to time to touch appealing tangibles with the body.
ud3.8:5.2: An alms-gathering monk, venerable friends, walking for alms is venerated, respected, revered, honoured, and esteemed.
ud3.8:5.3: Now, venerable friends, we too should be alms-gatherers,
ud3.8:5.4: and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to see appealing forms with the eye; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to hear appealing sounds with the ear; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to smell appealing smells with the nose; and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to taste appealing flavours with the tongue;
ud3.8:5.5: and we also will get the opportunity from time to time to touch appealing tangibles with the body;
ud3.8:5.6: and walking for alms we also will be venerated, respected, revered, honoured, and esteemed.’
ud3.8:5.7: This is the conversation, reverend Sir, that was left unfinished, then the Fortunate One arrived.”
ud3.8:6.1: “This is certainly not suitable, monks, for you sons of good family who through faith have gone forth from the home to homelessness, that you should talk such talk.
ud3.8:6.2: When you have assembled together, monks, there are two things that you ought to do:
ud3.8:6.3: talk about the Dhamma, or maintain noble silence.”
ud3.8:7.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud3.8:8.3: Such a one the devas envy,
ud3.8:8.4: But not if [he is] dependent on becoming famous.”
